Okay, sorry. Good evening chair and members of the school board. My name is Allie Reynolds and I'm with Girls on the Run Greater Richmond. I'm also a graduate of Henrico County Public Schools Hermitage High School class of 2007, not to age myself. I'm here tonight to share our appreciation for your continued commitment to supporting the whole child, not just academic success, but also emotional and social well-being. We are grateful to partner with schools across Henrico County and we truly value the trust you place in us to serve your students.

In Henrico County, we know that your vision is to empower every learner, and we see that value come to life in ways that you invest in programs and partnerships that help students feel seen, supported, and connected. That is exactly where Girls on the Run fits in. Girls on the Run is an after-school program for girls in third through eighth grade that uses a research-based curriculum to build social-emotional skills through movement, conversation, and connection.

Over 10 weeks, with the mentorship of trained volunteer coaches, many of whom are teachers, parents, and community members, girls grow in areas such as confidence, emotion management, healthy relationship building, and decision-making. And along the way, they begin to recognize something powerful, their own inner strength.

Across Greater Richmond, we are seeing the impact firsthand. This year alone in Henrico County, we have served 350 girls across 24 schools with support of 94 volunteer coaches. 99% of our GOATER girls reported that they felt their coaches cared about them, and 95% of participants reported increased confidence after completing the program.

But the numbers only tell part of that story. We continue to hear powerful feedback from the coaches, principals, and families who participate in GOATER through HCPS, a testament to the lasting impact of the program. Joy Reed, principal of Ratcliffe Elementary, said, This was by far the most impactful opportunity that our students have had in my 10 years at Ratcliffe.

One HCPS mom said, Goder made my child feel part of something bigger than herself. And Whitney Beck, assistant principal at Colonial Trail and a Goder coach, said, this is my 22nd year in education and my fifth as a building administrator. Of the many different clubs and organizations I have been able to be a part of through my years in education, none has impacted me more personally than being a Goder coach.

I've had the great pleasure to get to know a group of 30 girls in a way that was not tied to behavior, academics, or both. In spending time working through intentional character development and workouts during practice, I was able to build meaningful connections with students I rarely get to spend time with in this way.

This is a great example of what we hear from coaches and teachers again and again. These small moments don't stay small. They carry into the classrooms, hallways, and homes. We are deeply grateful for your partnership in making this possible for students across our region. As you continue investing in the well-being of the whole child, we hope you'll help us bring girls on the run to even more students so every girl has the chance to grow in confidence, connection, and resilience.

How can you, in good conscience, talk about accountability and propose that work can be made up for full credit, regardless of whether an absence is excused or not? You aren't just blurring the lines. You're erasing them. What kind of message does that send?

What kind of message does that send to students? It says that their reason for not being present doesn't matter. Didn't do your homework? Don't go to class. Didn't study for the test? Don't go to class. Get an extra few days to make it up. What kind of message does that give to parents?

It says we don't value them as partners in making sure students attend class sessions and do their work on time as assigned. What kind of message does that send to teachers? It says that their time in planning, preparation, and execution to stay on pace isn't valuable.

Having to create makeup work and dragging out the grading period for materials adds to even more tasks on their already full plate.
